Yesterday, the US government announced an update to its list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices"; today, a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) spokesperson confirmed the ban also applies to robot vacuums.

The robot vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other well-known brands—but you can continue to use your existing products

The Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US, with media attention focused on humanoid robots. But intelligence gathering doesn't require legs—and neither does the FCC's robot ban. FCC Director of Media Relations Katie Gorscak confirmed to The Verge that the ban will cover robot vacuums. The authorities are not targeting the Roomba in your home, and companies may continue to import and sell already-approved models. However, the government claims future foreign robots pose a national security risk, and even robot vacuum companies have suddenly been asked to commit to manufacturing in the US.

The FCC says advanced robotic devices pose national security risks, and these risks apply equally to products generally considered harmless, such as robot vacuums, robotic lawn mowers, and more.

Unless a device is explicitly approved or manufactured domestically in the US, it may not be sold in the country.

This ban hits the robot vacuum market particularly hard, because top brands like Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own these products, you can continue to use them today—the FCC won't be showing up to confiscate your robot vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban develops, the robot vacuum market could see dramatic changes in the short term. If all of this feels familiar, it's because the recent ban on wireless routers followed the same pattern.

Will you continue to use your existing robot vacuum? Why? Let us know in the comments.
